messages:
support_ops: FYI — customer ACME (prod, us-west) reports large p95/p99 latency spikes on /v1/generate starting ~09:28 UTC. No error rate bump but p99 ~5-6s. Ticket #12345. Any correlating deploys or infra alerts?
kevin_sre: looking now, I see p95 jumped ~09:27. No GPU/CPU saturation. What stands out: prefix_cache miss_rate shot up around same time.
omean_runtime: can you paste the cache metrics? size/evictions/miss_rate?
support_ops: pasted quick metrics from prod span: 
```
prefix_cache.miss_rate: 0.63
prefix_cache.evictions_per_min: 420
prefix_cache.size_bytes: 12884901888  # ~12GB
prefix_cache.entries: 1_100_000
recent_request_samples: ["user:acct:542:prompt:abcd...", "user:acct:999:prompt:abcd..."]
```
kevin_sre: those evictions are wild. Miss rate before deploy was ~0.09. Something introduced key fragmentation / high churn.
maya_engineering: note: we had a runtime deploy at 09:20 (commit 9f4b2c). That commit touched cache_key_normalizer — added additional header normalization to help debugging. Possible we accidentally included ephemeral headers in key.
kevin_sre: that would explain it — ephemeral headers (x-request-id, debug-tick) will effectively make unique keys per request and trash the prefix cache. I'm spinning up a local repro with a replay.
owen_runtime: quick repro steps I used: low QPS single model with header injection in loop. Within 2 minutes miss_rate jumps similarly. Repro command: 
```
for i in {1..1000}; do curl -s -H "x-request-id: $RANDOM" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood/test; done
```
kevin_sre: confirmed. The normalizer concatenates headers into the key when they exist. Bug: it didn't filter ephemeral headers.
lia_support: customer wants ETA for mitigation — can we do hotfix/rollback?
maya_engineering: options: 1) rollback commit 9f4b2c (fast, but removes some intended debug info). 2) push hotfix that explicitly strips ephemeral headers from key builder (small patch). 3) temporary capacity bump + pre-warm hot prefixes while we fix. Recommend hotfix + canary.
kevin_sre: I'll prepare hotfix branch: hotfix/strip-ephemeral-headers. Plan: deploy to canary, monitor prefix_cache.miss_rate and p95. If canary shows drop, roll to prod. Also set env var REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=2000000 on prod as short-term relief.
kevin_sre: patch diff snippet: 
```
- key_parts.append(header_value)
+ if header_name not in EPHEMERAL_HEADER_SET:
+   key_parts.append(header_value)
```
incident-bot: deploy started: runtime/canary by kevin_sre at 09:54 UTC. CI passed.
kevin_sre: canary results after 3m: miss_rate -> 0.12 (from 0.63), p95 down to ~400ms. Evictions dropped.
owen_runtime: rolling to prod in waves, doubling canary traffic in 5m increments. Keeping REDWOOD_PREFIX_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES increased until rollout complete.
lia_support: I'll update customer with interim mitigation and ETA for full rollback if needed.
maya_engineering: will open a followup PR to add unit tests preventing ephemeral headers entering key, and add histogram alerts for sudden miss_rate increase. Postmortem will capture root cause, timeline, and action items.
support_ops: thanks team — customer notified, will keep ticket open until metrics stable for 30m.
kevin_sre: once prod rollout finishes, I'll revert temp capacity bump and close incident.
lia_support: noted, thanks.
